unit.sep: Represent spatial/time patterns,calculate relationships,compare mechanisms and evaluate evidence for applications.
unit.careers: Illustrative acoustics,communications,environmental assessment and optical design roles.
unit.focus: Terms used in waves; The wave equation; Properties of waves; Application of properties of waves in real life.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional poster confuses wavelength with period,says every night improves sound transmission,and treats hearing around a corner as proof of one cause or a clear road.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Spatial/time records,boundary speeds,quiet echo/corner options,conditional atmospheric gradients and environment/road cards.
unit.drivingQuestion: How are waves applicable in our day-to-day life? How do waves affect our environment?
unit.content: Terms used in waves; The wave equation; Properties of waves; Application of properties of waves in real life.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Learning to learn: as the learner searches for information on applications of reflection, refraction and diffraction of waves.
Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner searches for information on mitigation measures of the effects of waves on the environment (communities, ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).
unit.values: Unity: as the learners play different roles when carrying out experiments to investigate reflection of sound waves using the echo method.
unit.pcis:
Safety and security: as the learner appreciates some of the applications of waves related to safety in transport.
Environmental issues: as the learner searches for information on the effect of waves on the environment (communities, ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).

assessment.instructions: Independent40minutes:5readGWV13,15Section1,10Section2,5Section3,5check/submit. Use only final reference/prompts;no keys or hints. Actual outcome d demonstration needs separate observed approved activity;written models are conceptual evidence only.

sections.title: 1. Quantities and the wave equation
sections.prompt: From GWV13 draw a labelled spatial sketch and identify amplitude,peak-to-peak displacement,wavelength,period,frequency and propagation speed. Explain v=fλ as one wavelength per period. Calculate wavelengths/period in A/B and explain unchanged frequency at the stationary boundary. Calculate echo wall distance and explain factor2.
sections.exemplar: Amplitude0.020m,peak-to-peak0.040m,wavelength0.60m,period0.20s,f5Hz,v3m/s. Propagation advancesλ inT,soλ/T=fλ. Boundary wavelengths3m/2m,T0.10s,f10Hz both;speed/wavelength change,source frequency unchanged. Echo340×0.30/2=51m,out-and-back path.

sections.title: 2. Distinguish wave properties
sections.prompt: Draw a surface/normal reflection diagram for incident angle30° from normal;label reflected angle. For the warm-ground profile draw/justify ray bending and state why day/night alone is insufficient. Explain wavelength/gap ratio for the supplied sound and draw a diffraction path around a corner plus reflected alternative;state why hearing alone does not prove one cause.
sections.exemplar: Reflection30°from normal. Warm-ground speed faster below/slower above bends rays upward;actual gradient/wind/noise/geometry not established by clock time. λ/gap0.80/0.40=2 suggests substantial spreading,but hard-wall reflections may also contribute. Draw distinct reflection and around-edge models;these are conceptual,not actual demonstrations.

sections.title: 3. Applications and environmental evidence
sections.prompt: Explain one mirror/road benefit and limit. Distinguish coastal water-wave effects from underwater acoustic exposure,and request one relevant evidence item for each before a local mitigation decision. State why no written answer here proves actual echo/corner experiments,video viewing or a safe road/engineering verdict.
sections.exemplar: Mirrors reflect light to aid viewing but do not remove all blind spots. Water waves can move sediment/affect shores;need site/habitat/infrastructure conditions. Underwater sound can affect species/communication depending on exposure;need level/frequency/duration/species data. Qualified local assessment and actual observed activities are separate;no experiment or safety certification follows from supplied models.
